bioEffects.text: Radiation dose is one factor in long-term health risk. Space agencies track career dose limits over a lifetime of missions. Your exposures so far remain well inside those limits — this page reports the environment, and the medical team interprets what it means for you.
bioEffects.title: What this means for your health

monitoring.text: These instruments measure the radiation environment around the station: how many particles arrive, what kind, and how much energy they carry. Detector readings are environmental data — they do not measure anything inside your body.
monitoring.title: What the monitors measure

units.label: Dose (mSv)
units.meaning: Amount of radiation energy absorbed, adjusted for biological effect.

units.label: Dose rate (µSv/h)
units.meaning: How fast dose accumulates at this moment.

units.label: Neutron counts
units.meaning: How many uncharged particles the detector registered per campaign.

shielding.note: During a particle event alert, the crew moves to the shielded module until flight control clears the all-clear.

trend.label: Cumulative effective dose
trend.note: Rate roughly 0.19 mSv/day inside the station; EVA days add a temporary bump. The dip after day 140 reflects time in the shielded module.
